samples.summary: Removing the `readOnly` early return from `handleImageMouseDown` makes the capture-phase handler swallow image mousedowns in view-only mode, so TextEditor's read-only link-follow path never records the href — a hyperlinked image that used to open its link on click in a shared/viewer document now does nothing.
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1667 `if (this.readOnly) { this.readOnlyPendingLinkHref = this.getLinkHrefAtMouse(e) ?? null; }` and the mouseup that consumes it at text-editor.ts:1991 only run if TextEditor's bubble-phase mousedown listener is reached. editor.ts:2586-2595 now calls `e.stopPropagation(); e.stopImmediatePropagation();` on any image-body hit in read-only too (the `if (readOnly) return;` at the top of `handleImageMouseDown` was deleted), so a click on an image inline carrying a link style never sets `readOnlyPendingLinkHref`. The same blockage also removes the ability to start a read-only drag-selection on top of an image.

samples.summary: The new "every mutation that shifts offsets clears the image selection" invariant has entry points outside `editor.ts` that bypass `clearImageSelectionForMutation()` — most concretely `FindReplaceState`, which the frontend drives directly against the Doc.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-find-bar.tsx:118 `state.replaceActive(replacement);` and :126 `state.replaceAll(replacement);` call into packages/docs/src/view/find-replace.ts:61/69 → `replaceMatch` (find-replace.ts:78), which deletes+inserts text of a different length and shifts every following offset. Nothing on that path routes through `clearImageSelectionForMutation` (editor.ts:1275), so a click-selected image's `(blockId, offset)` can end up naming a different image inline — and `imageSelectionProvider` (editor.ts:2307) only re-validates that *an* image sits at the offset, so a subsequent Cmd+X copies and deletes the wrong picture. `undoFn`/`redoFn` (editor.ts:2083, 2115) and the table row/column ops (editor.ts:3578-3627) are further unguarded entry points of the same shape.

samples.summary: `handleImageHover` was never read-only gated because an image could not previously be selected in read-only; now it can, so a viewer gets nwse-/ew-resize cursors over invisible handle zones for a resize the editor refuses.
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2737-2750 `handleImageHover` checks only `imageResizeDrag` and `selectedImage`, then `canvas.style.cursor = cursorForHandle(handle)`. With the `readOnly` gate removed from `handleImageMouseDown` (editor.ts:2538) `selectedImage` is now settable in read-only, while `drawImageSelection(..., { handles: !this.readOnly })` (doc-canvas.ts:683) draws no handles — so the cursor advertises a drag target that is neither drawn nor reachable (the resize branch is `!readOnly` gated at editor.ts:2559).

samples.summary: The context menu's Copy still keys off `getActiveSelection()` (text ranges only), so the read-only image copy the diff's comments claim the context menu offers is unreachable from the menu — selecting an image nulls the text range.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-context-menu.tsx:74 `const hasSelection = !!editor.getActiveSelection();` and :181 `const showCopy = hasSelection;`. `selectImageInline` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1256) does `selection.setRange(null)`, so with only an image selected `getActiveSelection()` returns null and Copy is hidden — contradicting the comments at editor.ts:1251 and editor.ts:2534 ("which is exactly where the context menu now offers Copy"). No `getSelectedImage()` reference exists anywhere in packages/frontend.

samples.summary: `selectImageInline` focuses the hidden textarea, breaking the standing "a read-only editor never takes focus on mount" behaviour; consumers that assume the viewer surface never grabs focus (scroll-into-view on focus, focus-ring/aria, host-level key handling) now see it focused.
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1258 `textEditorRef?.focus();` runs unconditionally, including from the read-only mousedown path (editor.ts:2592), whereas editor.ts:2841 deliberately does `if (!readOnly) textEditor.focus();`. Mutation is still blocked (text-editor.ts:639/692/768/894/1237/1462 readOnly guards), so this is behavioural rather than a write bypass.

samples.summary: Image mousedowns in read-only now call `stopImmediatePropagation`, which also starves document-level bubble listeners such as the context menu's outside-click close.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-context-menu.tsx:126 `document.addEventListener("mousedown", handleClick);` is a bubble-phase listener; packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2590 stops propagation from a container capture-phase handler on any image hit. In read-only the clipboard group can now be open (Copy), so clicking an image leaves the menu open instead of dismissing it.

finding.summary: Removing the `readOnly` early return from `handleImageMouseDown` makes the capture-phase handler swallow image mousedowns in view-only mode, so TextEditor's read-only link-follow path never records the href — a hyperlinked image that used to open its link on click in a shared/viewer document now does nothing.
finding.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1667 `if (this.readOnly) { this.readOnlyPendingLinkHref = this.getLinkHrefAtMouse(e) ?? null; }` and the mouseup that consumes it at text-editor.ts:1991 only run if TextEditor's bubble-phase mousedown listener is reached. editor.ts:2586-2595 now calls `e.stopPropagation(); e.stopImmediatePropagation();` on any image-body hit in read-only too (the `if (readOnly) return;` at the top of `handleImageMouseDown` was deleted), so a click on an image inline carrying a link style never sets `readOnlyPendingLinkHref`. verdict.reason: Verified independently. editor.ts:2538-2605 no longer has a readOnly early return; the image-body branch (2586-2596) calls stopPropagation/stopImmediatePropagation in read-only, and the handler is registered capture-phase on `container` (editor.ts:2606) while TextEditor's handleMouseDown is registered bubble-phase on the same container (text-editor.ts:577). So for any image-body hit in read-only, text-editor.ts:1667-1669 never sets readOnlyPendingLinkHref and the mouseup consumer at text-editor.ts:1991-2002 can never open the link; the read-only drag-selection start (text-editor.ts:1908-1920) is likewise unreachable over an image. Hyperlinked images are representable and user-reachable: image inlines are ordinary inlines (model/types.ts:516-525), and insertLink applies {href} across the whole range with no atomic-inline exclusion (editor.ts:3187, model/document.ts:407-412); getLinkHrefAtMouse resolves purely by offset (text-editor.ts:5565-5590). No alternative link-open path exists — window.open occurs only at text-editor.ts:1659 and :2000. This is a behaviour change breaking consumer sites outside the diff, violating the documented read-only contract at text-editor.ts:183-187; major under the blast-radius rubric (work silently skipped at another site).

finding.summary: The new "every mutation that shifts offsets clears the image selection" invariant has entry points outside `editor.ts` that bypass `clearImageSelectionForMutation()` — most concretely `FindReplaceState`, which the frontend drives directly against the Doc.
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-find-bar.tsx:118 `state.replaceActive(replacement);` and :126 `state.replaceAll(replacement);` call into packages/docs/src/view/find-replace.ts:61/69 → `replaceMatch` (find-replace.ts:78), which deletes+inserts text of a different length and shifts every following offset. Nothing on that path routes through `clearImageSelectionForMutation` (editor.ts:1275), so a click-selected image's `(blockId, offset)` can end up naming a different image inline — and `imageSelectionProvider` (editor.ts:2307) only re-validates that *an* image sits at the offset, so a subsequent Cmd+X copies and deletes the wrong picture. `undoFn`/`redoFn` (editor.ts:2083, 2115) and the table row/column ops (editor.ts:3578-3627) are further unguarded entry points of the same shape.

verdict.reason: Every claimed location checks out. `clearImageSelectionForMutation` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1275) documents the invariant that every offset-shifting mutation routes through it, but `FindReplaceState.replaceMatch` (packages/docs/src/view/find-replace.ts:78-87) mutates the Doc directly via deleteText/insertText with a different-length replacement and never touches the editor's image selection. That path is live: docs-find-bar.tsx:118/126 call replaceActive/replaceAll, and DocsFindBar is mounted at docs-view.tsx:600. The find bar is portalled to document.body (docs-find-bar.tsx:297) so it never triggers the container mousedown clear (editor.ts:2598-2604), and there is no blur-based clear; handleClose refocuses the editor (docs-find-bar.tsx:132-137) with the stale selection intact. `selectedImage` is a bare coordinate (editor.ts:1239) and both imageSelectionProvider (editor.ts:2307-2318) and deleteSelectedImageInline (editor.ts:2290-2295) only re-validate that *an* image sits at that offset, so a shifted offset naming a different image passes validation and a subsequent cut/delete hits the wrong picture. undoFn/redoFn (editor.ts:2083, 2115) likewise refresh the doc without clearing. This is an invariant introduced in one module bypassed by an entry point in another — in-lane and blocking at major.
